newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends up on speculative, fund buying.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends up on speculative, fund buying.

text.p: CME lumber futures rose on continued speculative demand based on a strong cash market and fund buying to close strong, traders said.

Lumber closed mostly $7.40 per tbf higher to $1.00 lower with only November off and May up $7.40 at $414.10 per tbf. July ended up $3.10 at $396.70. Distant January, which started the day with a one car open interest, rose the $10.00 daily limit on a single trade.
Futures ran up for as much as a $9.90 to $416.60 in May, its old contract high, near midsession on scattered demand before meeting commercial hedge selling, traders said.
"There had been some light mill selling today, the first we've seen of that," one trader said.

But the continued strong tone to the cash lumber market kept speculative buying firm. Cash prices should hold as most mills are reporting orders out three weeks. Futures remain at a discount to mill asking levels, currently in the $405 to $415 per tbf area, based on delivery charges, they added.
